notes: Protected abstract method every jagtheora peer subclass (OggPacket, OggPage, OggSyncState, OggStreamState, VorbisInfo, VorbisComment, VorbisBlock, DSPState, TheoraInfo, TheoraComment, SetupInfo, GranulePos, DecoderContext, Frame) must implement to release its native libtheora/libvorbis/libogg struct. Called only from dispose()/a().

Public no-arg disposer: if the peer handle is not already null/disposed (`!isDisposed()`), calls the abstract freeNative()/clear() to release native resources. Mirrors the finalize() safety-net below but is presumably meant to be called explicitly/deterministically by owners of these native-backed objects.

Overrides Object.finalize() (the actual `super.finalize()` call is commented out, so GC-driven finalization chaining is effectively disabled/dead here). Logic is identical in shape to dispose()/a() -- if not already disposed, calls dispose()/a() -- making this a redundant safety-net that disposes native resources if the owner forgot to call dispose() explicitly before GC. Declared with `@Throws(Throwable::class)` per the Java Object.finalize() contract, though the commented-out super call suggests this was left broken/incomplete during decompilation.
Returns `peer == 0L`. Used by dispose()/a() and finalize() as the disposed/null-handle guard before freeing native resources.

Private setter for the native peer/handle field. Never called from any Kotlin code in the repo (grep finds only the declaration) -- most likely written into the `peer` field directly by native (JNI) code via reflection or a cached field-id, which is a common pattern for these vendored jagtheora/jaclib peer wrapper classes rather than being dead code.

Protected external native static initializer run once in the companion object's init block when the SimplePeer class is first loaded -- likely loads/initializes the native libtheora/libvorbis/libogg JNI bridge shared by all peer subclasses.
